utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We should go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I please have exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 2365 displayed to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember giving a statement in September 2001 to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in the Milutinovic case, you made some adjustments to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I just have a look at page 2 of this statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I'm especially referring to your university degree, which is mentioned there. It is mentioned here that you obtained a degree as a physical training teacher. Did you ever obtain that degree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Then I was referring to -- it says here in the statement that you had a degree from the university in Sarajevo. Did you obtain that degree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you don't want to have any changes to your statement regarding your degree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm asking this because you told us in 2006 that you got in trouble with not obtaining a degree or there were some allegations about this. Could you just explain, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In 1991, I was at the physical training faculty in Sarajevo, and at the time the events started to happen on the territory of Bosnia; and although the faculty for physical training was on the Serb side, in the Serb area, pursuant to some decision by the Serbian university, a decision was passed whereby all the students who were at that faculty were to be proclaimed as having graduated from the faculty. So all the people attending, all the students attending who had not yet graduated but who were in their final stages, were recognised their graduate status. So I did not actually sit for my finals, but the Serbian university, in view of the events and circumstances, decided to grant a degree to all the students, the senior students at the faculty, so that is how I came to receive my degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation, could I ask that exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 2365 is being tendered, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 2365 shall be received as Exhibit P340. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have also public redacted version 2439, which we would seek to tender as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as a distinct part of that same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the public redacted version 65 ter 2439 shall be received as Exhibit P241. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you also testified twice already in the Milosevic case and in the Milutinovic case about the incidents in and around Mala Krusa in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript and the recording has wrongly identified the redacted -- or the other number, and the court officer will now correct that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The redacted version of the statement 65 ter 2365 shall be received as Exhibit P340, while the public redacted version shall be received as Exhibit P340-A. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The public redacted version, just for the record, has the 65 ter number 2439.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Witness, do you agree that both of your testimonies in the Milosevic and the Milutinovic case, together with your corrected statement, are true and accurate and would form the evidence which you would give if you would testify today orally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, I would seek to tender, therefore, 65 ter 2366 under seal. That's the transcript in the Milosevic case, as well as 2527. That's the public version of the Milosevic transcript containing a few redactions, as well as 65 ter number 5164, which is the Mos [Realtime transcript read in error, "mass"] transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by that last reference. Are you -- these three versions of the Milosevic transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I may have been ambiguous. The first two 65 ter numbers 2366 is the unredacted Milosevic transcript, which I would seek to tender; and the two 65 ter number 2527 is a partially redacted version, as far as I understand, so it's for the public; while the last number, 65 ter 5164, is the Milutinovic transcript, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, that is the thing that was confusing me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Milosevic [microphone not activated] ... unredacted will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P341. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The redacted version of the same transcript will be received as a sub-exhibit with that same number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P341-A. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript in the Milutinovic trial will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P342. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can read out the 65 ter number of the Mos transcript again. It's 5164, and we would seek also - I forgot to mention that - to tender this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That is being translated or recorded as Mos -- [microphone not activated] -- transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't understand, Your Honours, mass?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what's coming up in line 25, and it's what came up earlier when I said I didn't quite understand what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The 65 ter number of the Mos transcript, M-o-s, I meant the Milutinovic et all case, Your Honours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd better use Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. And we would seek to tender this under seal because it contains closed and private session testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, then the Milutinovic transcript will be received under seal, and that is Exhibit P342.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Milutinovic transcript is received under seal as Exhibit P342. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it not the case that the Milosevic transcript, the unredacted version, should be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe this is what we have done earlier this morning. We tendered one version under seal and the second version openly. I remember that Your Honours have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We gave a separate number to the redacted, but nobody mentioned seal for the main version, so Exhibit P341 will also be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exhibit P341 shall be received under seal. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would read out a summary of the witness testimony. The witness was a member of the 7th Company of the 23rd PJP Detachment, a unit based in Vojvodina, Serbia. In 1998, the witness's unit was deployed to Kosovo for six times, and in 1999, for five combat operations. In late March 1999, the witness's company was deployed in and around Mala Krusa during a mop-up operation. He describes the MUP and VJ units involved in that operation. The witness's unit handed over six Albanian men who were suspected of being KLA members to the MUP. He saw these men being marched to a nearby house from which he later heard gun-fire. He also handed over three men. Later, he saw the corpses of some men in the nearby house, which was also set on fire later. In Mala Krusa, he saw about 5.000 civilians moving through the village out of the combat area. These civilians were moved southwards later. He testified to be unaware about the massacre that took place in Mala Krusa on the 26th of March, 1999. He says to have heard about it later only after NATO troops entered Kosovo. Could we move into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To whom did Mr. Borisa Josipovic report to in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His immediate superior was the command of the PJP, Mr. Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And to whom did Mr. Obrad Stevanovic report to in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Obrad Stevanovic was the immediate superior or, rather, the chief of the public security sector was his superior, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On page 22 of your statement, you mention that the PJP units are intervention units. Could you explain what you mean by intervention units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's a very broad concept. Then I have to begin with 1991 or 1992 when they were first established and then go on from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let's start it from there. What is -- what do intervention units do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can't explain it just like that. In peace -- I can tell you in peace-time depending on the situation and so on and so forth, but in general terms, to prevent large-scale unrest and disturbance; and if there are any terrorist attacks, then they step in or for floods, fires, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that -- I withdraw that, sorry. Is it fair to say that PJP units would be manoeuvre units as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What are manoeuvre units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you're talking about 1999, then we worked to prevent Albanian terrorists, or, rather, we fought against the Albanian terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what is -- can you explain the term "manoeuvre"? What is specific about a unit who is described as a manoeuvre unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I think that the witness has explained what a manoeuvre unit is in response to the previous question and what the tasks of these units were and what they did, not to have to go and quote him on his answer to the previous questions. Line 30, lines 29 and 30, in fact. It's already been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't understand the question to have been specific to manoeuvre, so please carry on, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain, please, how a patch of the PJP looks like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you give me a picture, I can show you which one it is. We had special uniforms and special insignia and patches and special vests. The patches were on the left and right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 327 shown to this witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you please, if it comes up and if you see the patch worn by PJP, just please state the number for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I asked in the instructions that I submitted to the usher that, please, both pages would be displayed. We have currently only one here. Yes. I will come to the right exhibit later. This is obviously the wrong number here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This, I think, is half of the exhibit number that you gave but shown on the screens twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we can see the second page. I see now it's twice the same page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to talk now about the deployments of your unit from Vojvodina to Kosovo. Can you please tell me, how many kilometres is the distance from Subotica to Kosovo, let's say to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 600 kilometres, more or less, perhaps 550.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 00044 being displayed to this witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I mentioned already the combat operations in which you participated in 1998 and 1999. I would now - this is a map of Kosovo - simply - and I go here from page 5 of your witness statement - I would simply ask you to encircle the locations, which I take from your witness statements, where you were stationed or where you were performing combat. We just would need here one picture on the screen, not two. The usher will hand you a pen in a second. The first combat operation you mentioned in your statement, page 5, is on the road between Klina and Srbica. Could you just encircle once the map is coming up where that location is, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could enlarge the map as much as possible. We don't need -- even a little bit further. We just need to focus -- yes, a little bit, even, more. Yes, thank you. Could the usher please hand the witness a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle where the road between Klina and Srbica is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only approximate. I don't think I can locate it precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Perfect. Good enough. Please place a number 1 next to the circle you drew.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the first two operations in 1999 related to that road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I marked refers to 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the first two combat operations in which you participated in Kosovo, right? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The third operation - and you mentioned that, also, in your statement; I'm just going by your statement - was to liberate the road between Pec and Decani. Could you encircle that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mark a 2 next to the place, please. Thank you. And the third is the attacks on Jablanica. Please encircle Jablanica if you find it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not on the map, but I can try to locate it, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a three next to it. The next one is in the area of Prelip and Junik up to Baboloc. You were performing combat there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a 4 next to this place. And the last operation in 1998 was in the Junik and the nearby mountains. Could you encircle that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you marked a 5 next to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of 65 ter 00044 shall be received as Exhibit P343. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would now move to 1999 and would need the same map, not annotated again, please, for this witness in the same zoomed-in version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So moving on to 1999, I have here the first operation is the blockade of Mala Krusa-Zrze-Orahovac road. Please encircle the area, roughly, and mark a 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The second operation is to move towards Milanovici and take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You just marked a 2 next to it. The third one is to liberate the road, Pec-Kula-Rozaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a 3 next to it. Yes. The next one, the fourth one is to be in the area of Supot Lapodnica [phoen], lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You marked a 4 next to this place. And the last one I have here is Budakovo in the Suva Reka area. Could you mark a 5 next to this, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this map relating to operations witness participated in 1999, 65 ter 0044 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the second marked portion of 65 ter 00044 shall be received as Exhibit P3444. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We had just spoken about number 5 on this map, the operation in Budakovo area. Do you know when roughly this Budakovo operation was completed in 1999, which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That operation was completed around the 10th of May, 1999. The 9th or the 10th; I cannot tell you precisely. In any case, it was in the first half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And was it a success or failure for the 23rd PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We reached our goal. Therefore, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you now 65 ter 1993. When it will come up in a second, we will see that this relates to minutes of MUP staff briefing on the 11th of May, 1999, a day after or two days after you said the operation Budakovo was completed. And I only want to focus here on what the commander of your unit Bosko Josipovic, you mentioned his name earlier, participated in this meeting. If we can go to number 3 in these minutes. In English, it is page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was notified earlier that this exhibit was going to be used. Before the witness starts answering the Prosecutor's questions, I wanted to say that I believe this has nothing to do with this exhibit, and based on what I could see before, he can only read it for us, much the way we all could. I do not disagree with using this exhibit, but I object to it being tendered since I believe the witness has nothing to do with this document. There is no relation between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll explore that as the witness speaks about it. Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In B/C/S, we need to go to page 2, and we need to scroll to the bottom, the last two lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As I mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, that is not correct. I need to go, then, to number 3 in B/C/S, please, page 3 in B/C/S. Can we scroll up a little bit, please. Actually, this is the confusion. We have again twice the same English version here on the screen. I was referring to the B/C/S version. This is the second time this has happened this morning, Your Honours. We would need on the right-hand side of the screen page 2 of the B/C/S version - yes, thank you - and I said we need to go to the bottom. I'm sorry. We need to go -- this is page 3 here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want one page earlier in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah, I said page 2. I said page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Doesn't matter what you said. It's what we now need to find the right thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, we see here the commander of the 23rd PJP makes a comment. And you were earlier telling us about Budakovo. Could you just read the last two lines, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in the English version, we need to scroll up a little bit so that Your Honours can read it. Yes, thank you. The first two hyphens I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you comment upon what your commander is reporting here at this meeting? Is this a true and accurate reflection since you participated in this operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is what happened, at first with some difficulty, but then later on the operation was successfully completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why is your commander reporting this here at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it was standard procedure to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation, I would seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You maintain your objection, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. I believe the witness confirmed that he had nothing to do with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The minutes will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1993 shall be received as Exhibit P345. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just want to state for the record, I hope that the objection time doesn't count for my examination time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The objection time does. Everything counts for time, Mr. Neuner, but as you know we do not have a stopwatch. Keep moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would now ask that exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 4093 is being displayed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here it's from the 15th of July, 1998, and my first question is: Who had the power to send PJP units to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The PJP units were sent by the chief of the PJP, Mr. Obradovic, in principle. However, that was probably agreed upon at higher levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we look here at the authority issuing the document, we see it's the Public Security Department of MUP Serbia. Could you explain who headed that department in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we see among the addresses here, it says to the SUP, and one of the SUPs is mentioned here is Subotica. Could you explain what SUPs -- or what he says, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a secretariat of the internal affairs -- of internal affairs in that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which PJP unit was coming from that town, if any?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 23rd Detachment, the 7th Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here, and I'm just reading out a portion: "In order to assist the secretariats of internal affairs in carrying out special tasks ... mobilise and dispatch members of the 23rd ... Detachment of the PJP ..." And the second hyphen reads: "To Djakovica - 500 members ..." Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see here that from our town, only two platoons were sent, which means that some of our men had already gone down there and that this was a regular shift rotation. Throughout 1998, we kept going back and forth. These two were probably on leave and then were being sent back, or they were supposed to replace the men in the field. I cannot recall precisely what the situation was at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask with this explanation to tender this document, 4093.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm informed -- I'm sorry. It is tendered as 131, as Exhibit 131. I don't want to confuse the record here. Yes, I got confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you the next document, 65 ter 4132. So who had the power to rotate PJP units in Kosovo, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I have already said, the same person who planned operations. That person was in charge of rotation, as well, that is to say the Command of the PJP and the senior levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see the document is dated from the 4th of November, 1999, and I'm just reading out a portion here, starting at the second paragraph: "The engagement of members of the --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to say, but I'm just informed by my case manager that this document is already tendered as well. Therefore, I see, also, my learned colleague's on his feet. I would, therefore, just withdraw the document. I apologise for having it introduced, in the sake of time, to save -- in the interest of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the present exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is 136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I confirm that the 65 ter 4132 is already P136. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This document now I want to have displayed in any case, 40 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the parties agreed mutually to have this exhibit admitted in the pre-trial phase. What is unclear to me is whether my colleague intends to present this now or not. Another thing: The date stated, the date should be the 4th of February, 1999, instead of November. That should be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As I understand it, this is an exhibit already in the trial, having been admitted pre-trial by order, and Mr. Djurdjic is correct about the date, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe I've introduced it as 4 February 1999, but I've moved on anyway, Your Honours. In the interest of time, I wanted to have 4095, 65 ter 4095 being displayed. Could the document in the English version be enlarged a little bit, and in the B/C/S version, I know that the handwriting is partially cut off. We would need the upper part of the document including the handwriting, please. It could still be enlarged a little bit. I just need the handwriting in the upper part of that. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My first question is, the sender here is the RJB in Belgrade. Could you explain to Their Honours what the RJB is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Public Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who headed the Public Security Sector in 1999, 21 March, when this document was issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here, and I'm just reading the first line, that -- the first main paragraph: "In order to carry out ... tasks ... dispatch members of the ... 23rd ... PJP detachment ..." And the second hyphen in the text below reads: "To the Djakovica SUP ..." and then certain companies are listed, and the name "Subotica" is mentioned. Could you explain me what is being ordered here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is standard procedure upon arrival of a dispatch, whereby it is stated that a PJP unit is going to be engaged, stating where it should go and what the expected time of arrival is, as well as what the equipment that we'll need and the length of stay. This was a standard form of dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the handwriting on the upper right-hand part in the original. Here, a couple of handwritings; could you tell me first, what does the handwriting on the upper left mean, the one word there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Zinajic," and then "Radosavljevic," and "Zec." As for the fourth remark, I can't say whose handwriting or signature it is. In any case, the chief of secretariat had the officers engaged in this task to sign this. They signed the document as received.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The chief of which secretariat are you referring to here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The secretariat in our town, and it is Mr. Radovan Kinezovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the name of the town, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what was the position of Mr. Zinajic in 1999 March in the SUP Subotica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the chief of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the position of Mr. Zec, please, in that SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zec was the chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you give us the position of Mr. Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Radosavljevic was with the PJP. He was in charge of all the operational aspects that had to be taken care of in our town, that is to say, food, equipment, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document now and ask you to remember the dispatch number, which is 587, and the date, which is 21 March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 4095 shall be received as Exhibit P346. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is 4207, dating 22 March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, if you look at the reference line, below the name Belgrade, it is mentioned, it says here: Reference RJB, Dispatch 587 of 21 March. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we see the addressee of that document is the police administration. Where is this police administration located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the second addressee is the PJP Command. Where is that PJP command located, and who headed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The command of the PJP was located in Belgrade, and it was headed by Mr. Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you have a short look at it and just tell me what the purpose of that document is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Standard procedure. In relation to the previous one, the SUP of Zrenjanin was reporting on what had been, what had been done on the basis of the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So it's a reporting back related to the previous dispatch number 587, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 4207 is received as Exhibit P347. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document we displayed is a map, 615.06.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned at length in your statement, Witness, that you went on the 25th of March, 1999, from Djakovica towards a gas station in Zrze in the morning where you met a VJ officer. Do you remember this? That's page 8 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of meeting that VJ officer at the gas station in Zrze?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 25th in the morning at about 3.00 a.m., they woke us up to go on assignment. We set off at 5.00 a.m. in front of the SUP at Djakovica where the commander of the 23rd Divison, Mr. Borisa Josipovic, sent us with maps and designated operations and told us that we'd be met at the gas pump by a military man who would take us to the area where a company was assigned to set up a blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just take the pen and just draw a dot for Your Honours' attention, a dot simply where Zrze is where you met this man, the VJ officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now interested whether your -- where your company was stationed on that day. Where was the line of deployment of the 7th Company of the 23rd PJP? Could you draw the line of deployment on the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to explain this. Our area of responsibility was from Rogovo to Mala Krusa, but from the road to Rogovo, we had nobody there because it was an open space and there was no need to deploy anyone there, so we had the security zone, when we -- which was our area of responsibility, and then we had the place we were actually located in, and that was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether north of Zrze also some troops were stationed, and which troops, or in and around Zrze.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no north. It was just up, down, left, right, so I can't really tell you that way. I don't know where north is or where south is. Could you put the question differently?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the road where you drew already here your -- where your unit was deployed. First of all, mark a 1 next to this, and my only question, was along that road also other parts of your unit stationed, and if, so where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were stationed -- well, if we're talking about the 23rd Divison or a detachment, are we? Are we talking about the 23rd Detachment? All right, then they were here: Bela Crvka towards Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: All right. First of all, can you mark where your unit, the 7th Company was located, can you mark a 1 next to this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the second line where you drew, do you know which company was located there, and once you have given us the answer, could you draw a 2 next to the line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zrenjanin, Sombor, and whether anybody else took part, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, and these are the companies from these towns, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned the open space on the road where your unit was deployed. Could you tell me who was in between Zrze and the most leftern [sic] part of the road which was held by your unit? Was there any unit in between deployed, and if so, which unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the local police and the tank belonging to the Army of Yugoslavia. The tank was here, and these positions from one point to the next were held by the police, the police station, in fact, or the local policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark at the line you just drew a number 3 indicating where the local police was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And to the right, the lower right of Mala Krusa where the end of your unit's deployment was, who was being deployed there? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The local policemen were at positions next to us, holding the positions for the elevations above us, three tanks of the Army of Yugoslavia, and the Nis PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you first of all mark a number 4 where you believe that the local police was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And a number 5 where the Nis PJP was deployed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the number 6 where the tanks were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you mentioned in the Zrze area there was a tank. Could you indicate again where the tank there was and mark a 7 next to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, within this disposition, the village of Mala Krusa, which unit had the village of Mala Krusa in its AOR on the 25th of March and on the following days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depends how you look at it. We only set up the blockade line. We didn't enter any settlements. Now, the area of responsibility was ours, that's true, but for the blockade of the road. So we didn't have any troops there. We didn't, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And with "we," which unit are you referring to? The 7th Company? Can you just clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the 7th Company. I'm talking about us, so when I say "we," I mean the 7th Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we see here that roughly from three sides are troops stationed in the area. What was the purpose of this operation? Can you explain to Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The purpose of this operation was that the terrorists who were in this large area, they kept cutting across the road, and it was our aim to separate the terrorists from -- to push them back towards this settlement here - I've indicated that on the map - for the civilian population to be pulled out from one side and to push them back towards the other, towards a sector where we would be able from different sides to surround them. And operations of this kind were underway all the time, in 1998 and in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have just encircled here the village of Milanovici. Can you mark a number 7 next to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is, just for explanation, you explained to us where all the operations were taking place. That's the follow-up operation after this operation that your unit participated in an attack on Milanovici; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. I said that all the operations that we waged, both in 1998 and in 1999, were conducted in the same way. We set up a blockade first --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just listen to my question. What I wanted to get from you is after you were completed with your operation in this -- along this road here where you laid out the position of your troops. My question was, and you said you were pushing people to -- you were pushing terrorists towards that location which you have encircled as number 8. My question was whether you were indeed later on with your unit moving towards what you encircled as number 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic? Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you now tell me, where was this civilian population moving out of that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the second or third day after the operation had begun, the civilian population - well, this is my assumption - they wandered around in the area, but on the second or third day, they began to leave the settlement and move towards the main road, come up on to the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you draw us with an arrow the direction of the movement of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were coming out of here, from here, and here, and were moving towards Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark next to all three arrows you drew a number 9, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of document number 615.06 shall be given Exhibit P348. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you assisted the Office of the Prosecutor in producing a more detailed map of that operation on a computer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would show you the map, would you be in a position to recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 2373 being displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is this the map that you assisted the OTP with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I, for Your Honours's information, seek to tender this document as well. It's a more detailed depiction of what the witness has just explained to Your Honours on the other map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Without the numbers? Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 2373 shall be received as Exhibit P349. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would now seek to have Exhibit 318 being displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Witness, you mentioned a couple of times tanks being deployed that day, in March 1999. I would now ask you to tell us which vehicles, tanks, whatsoever, you saw that day on the road -- on the roads or in the operations area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, we could maybe have page 2 of that exhibit being displayed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tanks were number 6, and there were vehicles belonging to the VJ similar to number 2 on the picture. Well, similar, not exactly like this, but similar. It was a combat vehicle but not this kind; similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, the tank number 6, would you know a number of the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the 55. I'm not sure, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you - and this is now moving away from the operation - if you know, explain a little bit, for example, what number 7, picture number 7 is? What type of the vehicle is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a heavy-duty vehicle, and we had one such vehicle for the transport of ammunition and food.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we go to page 3, and we can just use the left side of the screen to go to page 3, please, of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any vehicles here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognise number 9, but we didn't have one of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What type of vehicle is number 9, and who had such vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Novi Sad PJP Company had one such vehicle, and it's -- well, I can't really use the professional name, but it was a combat vehicle with 20-millimetre machine guns, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned a couple of times in your statement also BOV, vehicle such as BOV. Did you see any vehicles here on the pictures I showed you which are BOV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all of those were BOVs, these four and the previous ones. We would refer to them as BOVs. Now, whether that was the professional name for this type of vehicle, I don't know, but we referred to them as armoured combat vehicles, BOVs; and whenever there was an armoured vehicle with wheels, we referred to it as a BOV.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We need to be a little bit precise. Which numbers depicted here in front of you qualify as such a BOV? Could you just give the numbers for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nine, 10, 11, and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving on to the next exhibit; 2015 is the 65 ter number. We have discussed this operation in and around Mala Krusa a moment ago, and you have explained to us in your statement that it started on the 25th of March, 1999. I want to show you this document here now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have at the moment some seizing of the technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can move for an early break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have two options. One is to move to an early break or move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I would seek to move to an early break if the technology doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will break now and resume at 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we in private session? We need to be, don't we, for the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 2015 being displayed. That's the document we want to show at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you have explained in detail the operation in and around Mala Krusa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same objection. This witness has nothing to do with this document except that it was presented to him by the Prosecution, so we do consider that the document is relevant, but it can't be tendered through this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will see what emerges. Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is a document dating 23 March 1999, and the title is "Order to Provide Assistance to MUP in Crushing and Destroying Siptar Terrorist Forces in the Orahovac, Suva Reka, and Velika Krusa Sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you about number 4 of that document, and this is on page 2 in the English, the fourth-last paragraph in B/C/S, also page 2, please, in the first paragraph there. If you could read --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We need to go up in B/C/S, please, to the top of the -- yeah, the first paragraph. The witness can't read the headline. Yeah, and in English we need to scroll -- yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here: Decision, and it says: "I have decided: To support MUP forces in their attack ..." And the goal is then mentioned in the next paragraph: "To block the Siptar terrorist forces in the general area of the village of Brestovac ... Celine, Velika Krusa, Mala Krusa, Randubrava, Pirane, ..." et cetera, et cetera. Could you explain to us the documents from the 23rd of March, 1999, to which operation does that order relate to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document relates to the operation that I was -- that we were in together with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you say "we were in..." So the operation was carried out as ordered here? Is that what you want to say, or can you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't clarify it because this is not a document that we had. We had something different, and this is described in far greater detail here than the one we had. So there were many places that I was not in, and I don't actually know where they're located either, but in general terms, that would be the same operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look here at the villages mentioned: Velika Krusa and Mala Krusa, Bela Crkva. Are these places where your unit or your neighboring unit were deployed on the 25th of March and forth-following days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So can I take it that the order was carried out, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 2015 shall be received as Exhibit P350. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to straight move to the next document, 65 ter 99. We only need page 2 of that exhibit, and it's a picture, so we need one screen only.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement you explained to us that at some point in time, you set up a headquarter in Mala Krusa of your 7th Company. Can you explain -- you told us earlier you came in the morning of the 25th of March, 1999, to the area of Mala Krusa. What day did you finally set up your headquarter, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 25th, straight away, as soon as we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think I said we need page 2 of that exhibit. Could we please have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you on this picture see where you set up your headquarter, and if so, please encircle it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a number 1 next to this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And we were having you mark a map, a map and a road, which your troops controlled, the 7th Company. Could you indicate where on that map the road is your unit controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark at the right end of that straight line you drew a number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which village, if any, is depicted here in front of us, the picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Mala Krusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to come back to the house you marked as number 1. Which family, if any, was living in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a family living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do know the name, but I ask that I state it in closed session. I asked for that last time too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we move into private session? I forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you certainly have heard that in the course of this trial we are litigating an incident relating to a so-called hay barn massacre on the 26th of March, 1999, in Mala Krusa; and a video has been played in the course of that trial for Your Honours' information. That's Exhibit 298, time code 42:21 until 44:10. I'm not necessarily intending to play that video now. I'm just informing yourself about it. People --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are all familiar with all of the statements of this witness. He, on several occasions, stated that he had no knowledge of that. My learned friend, Mr. Neuner, is now telling us that he does not intend to show that video footage, but what is the point at all of referring to that incident when the witness stated clearly he had no knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have a good-faith basis to ask the witness questions about what his knowledge or not knowledge about this incident is, and it's relevant to this indictment in these proceedings, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But is it not his evidence that we have perceived that he has no knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct, but am I not allowed to ask him one or two questions about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But he says he has no knowledge, so what's the point, then, of -- are you in a position to take the view that, despite his evidence, he does have knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I intended to ask this witness who was present - as I understood his testimony, from the 25th until the 28th of March, 1999, at least, in this village - I intend to ask him which other units he believes have moved through this village. That's all I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That's -- exactly. I couldn't finish my question. I got an objection in the middle of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You were introducing the story about which he knows nothing, but what he may be able to tell you is what units were in the village on those particular days, quite independent of what may have happened in the village. So just move to the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you heard -- you told us that you were in the village in the time period 25th of March, early morning, until 28th of March, at least, 1999. Could you tell me, did in this time period, apart from the local MUP forces you mentioned, move any unit or parts thereof?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness already answered. Your Honour, he has already answered this question on several occasions, the same question, and I'm certain you are well familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Neuner. The answer you had is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The question from me, then, is: Did you control all excess routes in and out of the village of Mala Krusa, or was there a possibility that somebody could move in there from other directions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We controlled all access routes from the direction of the road, but on the flanks and from the back, we had no control of that. It could have happened that someone entered the area from one of those sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Once you learned later on, as you testified, about the massacre, what was your explanation what could have happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still assert that I did not hear such amount of firing that would have sufficed to kill about a hundred people as is alleged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. With me is Ms. Jelena Dzambazovic, member of the team, and there is another member who is absent because he is preparing our case. That person is the lead counsel, Dragoljub Djordjevic. We speak the same language, and I frequently forget about my pace. However, for the sake of interpretation, please focus on my question and provide as brief answers as possible, and also, please watch the movement of the cursor on your screen. If any of my questions appear to be unclear, please ask me to clarify, and I will gladly comply. May I address you with Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Reading your statements and looking at the data, I conclude that you are a policeman who honourably performed his duties during the missions in Kosovo and Metohija. Am I correct in saying that you were also commended for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document -- Prosecution Document 1505 on the 65 ter list. Could we please have page 2 displayed in the B/C/S and page 1 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, you stated that General Lukic was the commander of the staff and that he controlled the units which were sent to Kosovo and Metohija. Could you please read the paragraph with the Roman numeral II.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The staff's task is to plan, organise, and control the work and engagement of organisational units of the ministry, and also sent and attached units, in expressing terrorism in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this confirm what have you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please read out the next sentence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "In addition, the staff's task is to plan, organise, direct, and coordinate the work of organisational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija in carrying out complex special security operations ."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How about the last two paragraphs preceding item 2? It begins with: "The expanded staff ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs, centres and branches of the RDB in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the staff comprised both members of the state and public security sectors alongside what you've just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please read out the Roman numeral III of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In terms of work, the work of the staff and the situation -- security situation within the framework of tasks of the staff, the head of the staff is answerable to the minister to whom he needs to report on the security-related events, undertaken measures, and the results of those measures.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Djurdjic repeat his last question and the witness's last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't think the interpreters heard me, so I'll repeat the question. Does this paragraph regulate reporting and responsibility for the staff's work to the minister?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, may we have page 3 in the B/C/S version, and it's still page 2 of the English. Thank you. Now, Witness, could you read out paragraph 6, Roman VI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "With the coming into force of this decision, the following shall cease to be valid: The Decision to Establish an Operational Staff, DT 01, number 4100595 of the 21st of April 1998, the Decision to Establish a Staff of the Ministry of the Interior for the AP of Kosovo and Metohija, ST 01 Strictly Confidential Number 1206/98 of the 15th of May, 1998, and the Decision on the Appointment of the Members of the Staff, that is, the head and members of the staff of the Ministry of the Interior for the AP of Kosovo and Metohija, ST 01, Strictly Confidential Number 1206/98-2 of the 11th of June, 1998."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, am I right in saying that by this decision, all the previous decisions are declared null and void, are no longer valid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, could you read out the signature, what it says at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlastimir Stojiljkovic, the then-minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now am I right in saying that in paragraph 5 of this decisions it is determined that on the basis of Article 72 of the law on Internal Affairs, that appointment of members to the staff shall be made in accordance with Article 72; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, am I also right in saying that in point 4, it says that the staff shall commence work on the 16th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we move on to another page, page 1, please. Am I right in stating that this decision, DT 01, and the number is 1580/98, was passed on the 16th of June, 1998, in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now going to start by questioning the witness with respect to his testimony here today, and in order for me to do that, may we have on our screens exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 5345, please; or P345 in English, and it should be P, P345 rather than 5345. So P345, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for this to come up on our screens, Witness, my first question to you is this: When was the first time you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that this is a document from the staff of the ministry and that the date of it is the 11th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I also right in saying that it refers to a staff meeting of the ministry, a ministry staff meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, would you read out the first sentence underneath that. Which one are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "In the work of the meeting, the assistant minister of the interior, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic, was present at the meeting."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in stating that this gentleman took part or, rather, was present at the meeting but that he was not in fact a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the previous document that, would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, am I right in stating that his position was assistant minister of the interior? That's what his post was; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, am I right in stating that the meeting was chaired by Major-General Sreten Lukic, the head of the staff, that he chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I state that in addition to the staff members, who are the first four persons on that list, that all the rest were commanders of the PJP units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in stating that these persons who were present report to the head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Djurdjic, did you want to tender as an exhibit the document which you had on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told it's already an exhibit. Can I have the exhibit number, then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just trying to do your job for you, Mr. Djurdjic, not very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You've already done my job because all the documents that I'm using are already in evidence, so that's how I'm conducting my cross-examination. Thank you. May we have another Prosecution exhibit, already admitted under number -- well, I'll have to give you -- the document number was 1492 under the 64 -- 65 ter list. It's a Prosecution document, P. But I'm sure it was attributed an exhibit number. I beg your pardon, but could my learned friend of the Prosecutor help me out. Did you use that document today?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was just trying to check it, and I don't have it in my binder, so I don't think I tendered it, but maybe my colleagues did. I was just informed that 1492 has not been used today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That is my mistake, then, and then what P -- what we need now is P131, which was exhibited today. And can we have page 2 in the B/C/S put up on our screens straight away, and it's page 3 of the English. There seems to be something wrong, but it was under the 65 ter list. It was 1493 of the 15th of July, 1998. This is 14 -- number 1493, and I was told that that has not been used. 131 is the number. My associate has found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we were saying, would you look at page 2 of the Serbian version and page 3 in English, although there isn't a translation; but for what I want to ask next, may we look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you focus on the end of the page where it says who sent this telegram. Am I right in stating that it says there, in addition to assistant minister, it says PO written in pencil; and am I right in saying that the person who signed wasn't Vlastimir Djordjevic; it was somebody signing for; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, there are a number of documents like this, and at the end of the English translation, it should read not "signature and stamp," but "unknown signature and stamp," or "NN," "not known," because certainly somebody else signed this document because it says pursuant to the authorisation of, "po," or for, and if you look at the official translation into English, it would appear that the aforementioned person signed, which is not true. It's incorrect. Thank you. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, telegrams of this kind, dispatches of this kind, were they normal, standard practice? Was it the way in which the minister's orders were carried out in the sense of sending troops to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now just to make it quite clear to Their Honours and everybody else, logistics, all the logistics, including training, materiel and equipment, weapons and so on, training, as I said a moment ago. All that was done within the frameworks of the department that existed in the police administration in Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the engagement or deployment of the PJP and control and command in KiM and planning came under the responsibility of the staff pursuant to a decision from the minister; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in Exhibit P133, I don't have to ask any questions because we have the same problem coming up in 133 as we did in 131. So I have to ask the clerk to put page 2 of the B/C/S version, so I'd like page 2 of document P133 on our screens now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, is this the same as the previous document? It says P-o, "po," and then we have somebody else's signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And once again, my comment is that the English should be corrected and that it read NN, signed by hand, or not -- unknown signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I make the observation, Mr. Djurdjic, because it may save a lot of time, the Chamber does not understand the English translation to be mistaken in any way. The first document, Exhibit P131, said for assistant minister. This document says per procurationem, or per proc, as it's usually abbreviated. It's saying on behalf of, or for, and then somebody signs it who is not the assistant minister, but somebody else signs. So in the ordinary English rendering, this is saying it's not the assistant minister who's signing. It's saying somebody else has signed for the assistant minister. So if that's an issue you have with a number of documents, I don't think you need to bother about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You know why I did that? Because the lower half where we can see the author of the document, in that document it does say Vlastimir Djordjevic type-written, and then somebody signed. So in addition to this type-written name, you have the signature. But you're quite right, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, now, the other exhibits relating to these telegrams, I'm not going to show anymore. You've already explained that to us, but I'd like to move on now and look at exhibit according to the 65 ter list, and it is P2015, and that is number P390 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have the first page of that document pulled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right in saying that in the heading it says, "Joint Command for KiM"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will read out the order. It says: "Order to provide assistance to the MUP in crushing and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If there was a joint command, wasn't it supposed to provide support to itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it obvious that a command of sorts is ordering something in support of MUP forces for its own respective units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could we please move to item 2 of the document. Witness, am I right in saying that item 2 contains tasks for the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does the PRK stand for Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'll not well versed in military abbreviations; therefore, I can't say with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: However, you said that it's a military abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because the entire text, the entire document is from the armed forces. It doesn't concern the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us go to page 5 or the last page in the English, and page 5 in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This document is not signed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please limit your answers to the facts that you are certain of. If there's something you don't know, please tell me so. Today, you said that General Obrad Stevanovic was the PJP commander. When does that piece of information date back to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that from the period prior to 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I truly can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When we were going through this document, did you see that his title is actually assistant minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Given the composition of those in attendance and the fact who reported on it, would he have reported, also, to someone as the PJP commander as regards the operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, obviously not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right, then, that you link General Stevanovic with the public security sector having in mind his previous positions, rather than the position of the assistant minister of interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was on two different posts, but I'm not certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what I wanted to ask you. You said today concerning the 25th of March, 1999, operation, you said that your company commander received a decision about your activities. Were you present when he received that decision.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. May I add something? It wasn't a decision. It was a map on the entire operation and disposition of forces, communication points, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since you say you were next to him when he received it, why were you there? What was your function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each company has its command post. I was there to assist. On occasion, I drove him. Sometimes I distributed food. But I was at the location where our company command post was as a regular policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm asking you this because you said you were familiar with the operation, and you keep referring to only one part, one side of the operation, the one that you are familiar with. Do you know that from a different direction, from Orahovac, there was an operation underway at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
