utterances.text: I do know that, but I was only referring to the things that I'm certain of, that I know 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that between the 25th and the 28th, you were not along the stretch of the road towards Bela Crkva, which you marked on the map today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was at the line of the blockade for all four to five [Realtime transcript read in error, "45"] days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, what you marked on the map is not direct knowledge on your part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had that on the map. We knew where the positions of the other participants were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right in saying that during 1998 and 1999, you never received an order from your superiors to kill Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right in saying that during 1998 and 1999 when you were in Kosovo and Metohija, you never an order to expel Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that you never received an order to rob Albanian civilians, to destroy their property, to destroy and bring down mosques in 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that you, while you were in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999, you never killed a single Albanian civilian; you never expelled a single Albanian civilian; you never robbed anyone; you never set anything on fire, be it a private being or a religious facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that from your superiors, you received orders to keep in mind the safety and take care of Albanian civilians and to help them to the extent possible, and that this is what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not examine you regarding your previous testimonies, but I would like to refer to some other things I want to ask you about which you haven't mentioned so far so as to save time and not to examine you about the things which were already admitted. Witness, am I right in saying that the local reservists were protecting themselves in their villages because there weren't enough police to protect them and they felt a need to enjoy such protection; therefore, they decided to protect themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that on that occasion, you did not conduct an operation of besieging any Albanian villages but that you actually developed along the line of blockade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the goal of the operation between the 25th and the 28th or the 29th of March, 1999, was to search the terrain where there were members of the KLA in order to arrest them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the operation was not directed at Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I have to go back to some issues which were not raised today but are nonetheless of interest to me. You provided your first statement in 2001. Going through that statement, I saw that one of the people who talked to you was Mr. Philip Coo. I want to ask you this: Did he introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean the first statement from September 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The two people that were there introduced themselves. One of them appeared subsequently as well, whilst the other person appeared only that one time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in that person who was there the one time. Did he tell you what his profession is and what he is expert in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you worked with the maps shown here today with him or with someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't with him. It was with Peter Steward.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pardon me, Your Honour, but I'm being warned by my colleague that a wrong exhibit number was entered in the transcript at page 55, line 4. It says P2015, whereas it should be P390. That's what it was entered in the transcript, but rather, it should be P350 from the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that in 1998 and 1999, the relationship between the MUP and the army was such that there was no superior-subordinate relationship? These were two separate organisations with their own respective systems of control.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the PJP units in the cases envisaged by the decision on their establishment were supposed to be active in the entire territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the equipment of PJP members was the same when you were sent to Kosovo and when you worked in territories outside Kosovo, that is to say, in Serbia itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the uniforms that you wore in Kosovo and Metohija were the same uniforms you were wearing when you were deployed in places outside of Kosovo and Metohija but within the frameworks of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise, but when are we due for a break? I wasn't looking at the clock. Should we take a break now, or shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would normally have a break in the next 10 or 15 minutes, but if you would like a break now, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was just asking you because I know that we started a little earlier, but, yes, I can continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, am I right in saying that the PJP units were set up by SP 01 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat the number of that decision, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- of the 1st of August, 1993, by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I can't tell you about the decision number, the dates, and things like that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the PJP units were established on the principle of rallying men together, that is to say, policemen together, and those policemen were people who went around performing their regular police duties in the organisational units of the SUP, such as traffic policemen, members of the patrol, the fire Brigade and so on and so forth; and when they were called up, then they become members of the PJP. Would I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when the policemen complete their assignment in the PJP, they go back to their regular police duties. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, am I right in saying that the tasks and assignments of the PJP were those determined by the minister once he makes the decision to engage the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that, as a rule, they were the following tasks and assignments, among others, of course: To keep public law and order at mass public rallies; and then to implement measures for extraordinary security or special security measures; the establishment of law and order when law and order has been upset to any great extent; then, the detection and uncovering of sabotage and other hostile groups and individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying, Witness, that a PJP unit, when it is sent on assignment outside its original unit, that it is placed under the command of the unit to which it has been sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer you if you put the question in that way. Could you ask the question differently?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Am I right in saying that part of a unit or whole unit which, pursuant to a ministerial decision, is sent outside the realm of the original secretariat, that it then comes under the command of the individual who the minister has assigned to lead the operation to which the PJP unit has been sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when we speak of police check-points, am I right in saying that those check-points are established and set up in order to detect illegal possession of arms, the smuggling of arms and drugs, the smuggling of looted items, vehicles, stolen items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Among its other duties, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that at those check-points, there is no discrimination based on ethnicity and that check-points exercise their duties in Kosovo and Metohija regardless of ethnic affiliation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I was, that's right. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm just asking you about, about what you know and where you were. If you don't know and weren't somewhere, then just tell me and I'll move on because I'm not asking for an opinion. I'm just asking for what you know or do not know. Am I right in saying that when the operation took place from the 25th to the 29th of March, you did not expect this kind of civilian influx into the area in which you were located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. We weren't expecting that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that the civilians went out onto the main road linking Prizren and Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that those civilians left their homes for security and safety reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that during the time of the blockade, that is to say from the 25th to the 29th, that you had an exchange of fire with the KLA members, that there was cross-fire between you and them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's clear one more thing up. When you drew the location of the blockade and how far it stretched, was that something that the police would do regularly when searching the terrain and when trying to catch any sabotage and terrorist units or individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying, and bearing in mind the questions asked today with respect to the six KLA members who were handed over to you first, that a rifle, a Chinese-manufactured rifle was found on them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that in the second group of individuals, or, rather, there were three persons; that they, too, had insignia patches denoting them to be members of the KLA, Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I think this would be a good time to break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will break now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before we continue, my associate has just told me that in the transcript, line 58, it says -- or, rather, page 58, line 1, it says 45 days. I'm going to ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true and correct that the operation that you took part in in the blockade from the 25th to the 29th of March lasted for four or five days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So now we can correct that in the transcript. Witness, I'd like to move on to another area now please, and we'll come back to the one we are discussing. Does John Sweeney seem familiar? Is it a familiar name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Although it is somewhere at the back of my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So can I take it, then, that you don't remember ever having talked to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that Mr. Sweeney, or, rather, do you know that this same man, Mr. Sweeney, who is a British journalist, claims that he talked to (redacted)? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you've jogged my memory. Yes, I do know that journalist, and I do know that he talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this journalist, Mr. Sweeney, claimed that (redacted) told him that he offered you a Mercedes if you were to allow him to flee from him home, so am I right in saying that that is not true?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just suggest that we go into private session, Your Honours, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we certainly should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right in saying that save for the three people for whom you said committed crimes while you were in Kosovo and Metohija in 1999, no other MUP member that you saw committed a crime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know whether the unit -- whether a unit for special operations was a part of the state security sector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that the women and children that were at the train station in Mala Krusa were completely safe and protected; that is to say that you took care of them, provided food and other necessities that you had, and that in essence there was only one policeman placed there to take care of the children who were running across the road between Djakovica and Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that among the civilians there were KLA members who had infiltrated such groups and that your orders were not to engage such individuals so as to avoid civilian casualties, although you knew that there were some KLA members who had changed into civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I fail to understand the question. Could you put it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Even though you knew that certain KLA members changed into civilian clothes and mingled with the civilians, your orders were not to open fire so as to avoid any civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right in saying that your task was to hand over captured KLA members to the crime department specialists in order to pursue the procedure envisaged by law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that on that day in March 1999, you handed the captured KLA members over so as to follow up on the legal and lawful procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We handed them over to the Prizren SUP people who were competent for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You didn't even dream of anything happening to those prisoners when you were doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that many able-bodied men after controls were released and let free to go to Prizren, they were not detained by the police if it was confirmed that they were not KLA members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain although I know how it came about that you gave the statement, but it is not written in the first-person singular and several places; in particular in the first statement of 2001, I come across the phrase "my men" or "my people." When we see that in English, as well. Can you tell us what did you understand by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not mine as such, but I meant to say all of the policemen from our detachment, our company, our Subotica company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you had in mind your work-mates from the 7th Company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of the Subotica PJP. The statement was first drafted in their language and then translated back into ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. This concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Neuner, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked today about Obrad Stevanovic by my learned colleague. Have you ever met Mr. Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once, when there were demonstrations. It had nothing to do with 1999. I only saw him there. I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me where the demonstration was and in which year it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade, in 2000, I believe. I don't know exactly. It may have been 1999 or 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by somebody, or he was just visiting on his own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you again clarify: In 1999, to whom did Mr. Obrad Stevanovic report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic's superior was Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. He held two positions. He was post PJP commander and assistant minister. As a matter of fact, he had two superiors: The minister and the chief of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you know, on which issues did Mr. Stevanovic report to Mr. Djordjevic, only if you know. I'm not asking you to speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wanted to come back briefly to the six gentlemen from the KLA which were handed over to the three local policemen from the SUP Prizren. My learned colleague had asked whether -- and you had confirmed that a Chinese rifle was found with one of these six persons. Could you tell me, at the time you handed these six gentlemen over to the local policemen, did the gentleman still have the Chinese weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They did not have any weapons on them. They were searched and handed over without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were asked about --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we maybe move into private session for a second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I've just a few questions relating to uniforms now. My colleague addressed the issue of uniforms being worn by PJPs. Could you describe the ordinary colour of uniforms worn by PJPs in 1999 and 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And while the witness is doing that, I would ask that Exhibit 325 is being displayed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just describe before the -- while the exhibit appears.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniforms worn by the PJP were green, yellow camouflage uniforms. It is picture number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me which other uniforms you can find here, as well, on this photo-board and who wore them, if you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Picture 4, it was worn by the local police, the local reservists. Photograph 8; the Frenki's men or the JSO; photograph 6 is a combination of the PJP uniform, but it also had the so-called urban environment uniforms; however, the vests depicted were part of our regular uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And "our regular uniform" is the uniform of the PJP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Coming back to number 8, you said it is worn by the JSO of Frenki. What is "JSO" standing for, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Special operations unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was commanding the special operations unit in 1999, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him as Frenki. I don't know his full first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you spell, for the record, Frenki?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As it is on the screen. It is correct. F-r-e-n-k-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we now have Exhibit 327, please, and if you see on the next exhibit the insignias --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think it is a two-page exhibit, actually. If we could have ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you find here any insignia from the JSO on it? If not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only numbers 13 and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thirteen, we had --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As well as number 4, the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you say what the patch 12 -- which unit wore patch number 12?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the special anti-terrorist unit belonging to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who in 1999 headed the special anti-terrorist unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know under whose responsibility, overall responsibility, now, the special anti-terrorist unit fell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't know who commanded it and what its structure was. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I ask you whether the special anti-terrorist unit was under the VJ or under the MUP overall in 1999, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend, Mr. Neuner, got the answer that it was within the MUP structure but that he doesn't know who it belonged to or what body. Therefore, he's already answered the question, and the last question is, therefore, unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would have said that without any further question, the answer was the Ministry of the Interior. Are you being more specific than that in your latest question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't believe I have established that yet. I thought I was in the process of establishing that. My learned colleague has suggested it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm confusing question and answer. I see that now. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us to the best of your recollection, in 1999, was the special anti-terrorist unit under the roof and in the composition of the VJ or of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was part of the Ministry of the Interior. I did not encounter them, save for one occasion in 1998. In 1999, I did not see them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In 1998, could you tell us on which occasion you encountered them and what task, if any, and if you know, this unit was performing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I referred to 1998, on one occasion they were with us. We developed along the blockade line between Klina and Srbica, along that road, but they did not go into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know why they didn't go into action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were no attacks aimed at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that in case an attack would have been aimed along the line, Klina-Srbica, this unit would have been employed to counter that attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. Had there been any need for them to take action, they probably would have, but there was no need. I can't tell you precisely in which cases they would have gone into action and under what circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you seen their equipment, and if so, could you tell us what the difference between the equipment of an ordinary PJP policeman and special anti-terrorist unit member was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There wasn't much difference. They had infantry weapons, much as we did. There was nothing that would be very different to the equipment we had. They only had a different uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 326 on the screen for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You will see, these are different types of weapons. My first question would be, which weapon was used by your own unit, the PJPs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the right-hand side schematic, we had the weapon number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness has recognised on page 2 of that exhibit, weapon number 1, as the one being worn by his own unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me on page 2, meaning the right-hand side here, what weapon number 2 and, if you know, number 3 and 4 and so on is? If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe we have a third page. Maybe we could try the third page. I'm informed there are only two pages. If we could go to the first page, back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any weapons on the first page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only recognise the photograph number 2. It's a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which units would use such a mortar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every detachment had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're referring to PJP detachments; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for answering all my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you, and it's now possible for you to leave to return to your normal activities. The Chamber would like to thank you for your visit to The Hague and the assistance you've been able to give us. Thank you very much. The court officer will now show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome. Thank you, as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session. Given the hour, we have two or three minutes only. I think we would see no sense in attempting to start a new witness now. We will therefore adjourn until Monday to continue with the next witness. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of March, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
